# Sl3 Int Generated By Order Two And Three refuted

Resolved false: the Kourovka Archive answers 14.49 "No, it is not", citing Tamburini and Zucca, and
Nuzhin: `SL₃(ℤ)` is not generated by an element of order `2` and an element of order `3`. Source: E.
I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st
issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved Problems, Problem 14.49 (M. Conder); resolution:
M. C. Tamburini and P. Zucca, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. (9) 11 (2000), no. 1, 5-7; Ya. N. Nuzhin,
Math. Notes 70 (2001), no. 1-2, 71-78, Kourovka Archive, Problem 14.49 (answer: No, it is not;
SL_d(ℤ) is such a quotient for d ≥ 28).
